intro: West LA's heart is Sawtelle Japantown, a few walkable blocks of ramen counters, izakayas, dessert shops and pop-culture stores between Santa Monica and Olympic Boulevards. Around it, Pico and National have some of the Westside's best neighborhood bars.

to: Time Out: Best restaurants in Sawtelle Japantown
dla: Discover Los Angeles: A walking tour of Sawtelle Japantown
gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites we checked)

places.w: A Korean-Japanese cafe with house-roasted coffee and fresh-baked specialty pretzels.
places.o: A latte and the honey butter bread or a pretzel.

places.w: A cheerful all-day cafe with lots of vegan, vegetarian and high-protein options and plenty of seating.
places.o: A breakfast bowl and the beekeeper latte.

places.w: The ramen shop that put Sawtelle on the map, famous for tsukemen dipping noodles in a long-simmered pork broth.
places.o: Tsukemen, then try the even richer Annex across the street another day.

places.w: Customizable tantanmen noodles with spice levels from zero to six.
places.o: Start at level two.

places.w: Rich tonkotsu ramen with late hours and cheap rice bowls.
places.o: The kotteri ramen.

places.w: Cafeteria-style fresh udon with a line of just-fried tempura.
places.o: Pork udon and too much tempura.

places.w: Organic buckwheat soba made in many styles, with tempura fried to order.
places.o: Cold soba with a side of tempura.

places.w: A rare spot for Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki layered with yakisoba and a fried egg.
places.o: The classic okonomiyaki.

places.w: A refined yakiniku grill.
places.o: Beef tongue and a tasting set.

places.w: A lively izakaya known for Nagoya-style chicken wings and a big beer and sake list.
places.o: Tebasaki wings and a beer.

places.w: Edomae sushi sets at gentler prices than most omakase counters.
places.o: A nigiri set.

places.w: Family-run Vietnamese comfort food and a smart backup when Tsujita's line is long.
places.o: Pho or a rice plate.

places.w: Consistent modern Chinese with excellent soup dumplings.
places.o: Xiao long bao and dan dan noodles.

places.w: Stylish Thai street food from a sister-led kitchen, with a Bangkok-inspired mural.
places.o: Street noodles and the barbecue squid.

places.w: A Mexican bar with a great patio and inventive cocktails.
places.o: Birria tacos and a margarita.

places.w: Filipino rice and pancit combos, each with pandesal. Open Friday through Sunday.
places.o: A combo plate with Filipino spaghetti.

places.w: Travel-inspired ice cream flavors and house-made cones.
places.o: Ube malted crunch.

places.w: Fish-shaped taiyaki cones filled with soft serve.
places.o: Ube soft serve in a custard-filled taiyaki.

places.w: Sawtelle's oldest boba shop.
places.o: Classic milk tea and popcorn chicken.

places.w: A Japanese grocery with good bento and sushi, next to the Daiso housewares store.
places.o: A bento and a can of royal milk tea.

places.w: The pop-culture shop that helped start the modern Sawtelle scene, with a gallery for emerging artists.
places.o: Browse the toys and graphic novels, then the GR2 gallery.

places.w: Frank Gehry's first house design, built to show a Pop Art collection. View it from the street.
places.o: A quick stop on a Sawtelle walk.

places.w: A classy cocktail lounge with a small dance floor and local DJs on weekends.
places.o: A smoked old fashioned. Open Wednesday through Saturday.
